inline_comments.comment: `key="reload"` has no effect here. React only uses `key` for reconciliation of dynamically-generated lists (arrays). Elements inside a static `<>` Fragment are never reordered by React, so this key is meaningless. Note the existing zoom buttons (lines 88, 100, 112) follow the same anti-pattern, but the PR adds another instance of it. Remove `key="reload"` to avoid misleading future readers about the intent.

`onReloadStory` is added to an exported public type without a JSDoc comment. `PreviewProps` is consumed by external story authors and addon developers; a brief `/** If provided, renders a reload button in the toolbar that remounts the inline story via FORCE_REMOUNT. Only meaningful for inline stories. */` comment would make the prop's purpose and constraint discoverable in IDE hover tooltips without requiring a doc lookup.

The restriction to inline stories is non-obvious without explanation. An iframed docs story embeds an independent `<iframe>` that hosts its own preview and channel bridge; emitting `FORCE_REMOUNT` on the outer docs channel would not reach the iframe's preview listener. A short inline comment—e.g., `// Reload is only supported for inline stories; iframed stories manage their own preview channel`—would save future maintainers from having to rediscover this.

general_comments.comment: No stories covering the new reload button behavior were added, and none of the existing toolbar stories were extended to exercise it. The project rule requires that interactive components have story `play` functions that programmatically trigger the interaction so the open/active state is captured in visual regression tests. Concretely: `Preview.stories.tsx` should gain a `WithReloadButton` story (passing an `onReloadStory` callback) with a `play` function that clicks the button and asserts the callback was invoked; `Canvas.stories.tsx` should add a story that verifies `FORCE_REMOUNT` is emitted with the correct `storyId` payload when the button is clicked. The PR description's test checklist has all boxes unchecked, which confirms this gap.

There are no unit tests verifying the core behavior: that clicking the reload button emits `FORCE_REMOUNT` with the correct `{ storyId }` payload on the channel. Without this, a future refactor that breaks the event emission (e.g., wrong event name, missing storyId) would pass silently. A focused unit test for `Canvas.tsx` — mocking `docsContext.channel.emit` and asserting it is called with `FORCE_REMOUNT` and the story's `id` — would provide this regression protection.
